cases.purpose: Assert canonical operands and Linux priority/discard bits with every swapon syscall answered by seccomp notification, without enabling swap.
cases.oracle: util-linux 2.41 resolves an existing operand to its canonical path before swapon(2). Priority and discard flags are the Linux ABI values.
cases.comparison: Exact ordered syscall records for canonical paths, success responses, empty output, and unchanged /proc/swaps.
cases.script:
set -u
H=/opt/bashos-parity/harness/helpers/system-seccomp.py
D=/tmp/parity-case
mkf() { /usr/bin/dd if=/dev/zero of="$1" bs=64k count=16 status=none && /usr/sbin/mkswap -q "$1" >/dev/null; }
/usr/bin/mkdir -p /fixture "$D" || exit 125
mkf /fixture/plain && mkf /fixture/p0 && mkf /fixture/p1 && mkf /fixture/pmax && mkf /fixture/discard && mkf /fixture/both && mkf "$D/-name" && mkf "$D/s1" || exit 125
[[ $(type -t swapon) == builtin ]] || exit 125
/usr/bin/cat /proc/swaps > "$D/swapon-before" || exit 125
: > "$D/swapon-log"
PYTHONDONTWRITEBYTECODE=1 /usr/bin/python3 "$H" --notify swapon --reply swapon=0 --log-string swapon=0 --log-args swapon=1 --log "$D/swapon-log" -- "$BASH" --noprofile --norc -c '
  [[ $(type -t swapon) == builtin ]] || exit 125
  cd /tmp/parity-case || exit 125
  swapon /fixture/plain &&
  swapon -p 0 /fixture/p0 &&
  swapon -p 1 /fixture/p1 &&
  swapon -p 32767 /fixture/pmax &&
  swapon -d /fixture/discard &&
  swapon -d -p 5 /fixture/both &&
  swapon -- -name s1
' > "$D/swapon-out" 2> "$D/swapon-err" || exit $?
[[ ! -s "$D/swapon-out" && ! -s "$D/swapon-err" ]] || exit 1
/usr/bin/cat /proc/swaps | /usr/bin/cmp -s "$D/swapon-before" - || exit 1
/usr/bin/python3 - "$D/swapon-log" "$D" <<'PY_CHECK'
import json, sys
import os
base = sys.argv[2]
def rp(path):
    return os.path.realpath(path)
expected = [(rp('/fixture/plain'), 0), (rp('/fixture/p0'), 0x8000),
            (rp('/fixture/p1'), 0x8001), (rp('/fixture/pmax'), 0xffff),
            (rp('/fixture/discard'), 0x10000), (rp('/fixture/both'), 0x18005),
            (rp(os.path.join(base, '-name')), 0), (rp(os.path.join(base, 's1')), 0)]
with open(sys.argv[1]) as f:
    records = [json.loads(line) for line in f]
actual = [(r.get('string0'), r.get('arg1')) for r in records]
if actual != expected or any(r.get('syscall') != 'swapon' or r.get('reply') != 'value:0' for r in records):
    print('unexpected supervisor records:', records, file=sys.stderr)
    sys.exit(1)
PY_CHECK
